\chapter{At the Doctor}
\label{ch:te-at-the-doctor}
\hlchaptermodality{92}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say I have a cold, a wound or feel weak, and talk about medicine and the hospital.}

Complete TE-C92-weakness: tell a doctor what is wrong.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[jalubu]{\te{జలుబు} (jalubu) — a cold, a runny nose}

\label{lesson:TE-C92-cold-illness}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for where to, then the Telugu for have you eaten.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{జలుబు}}
\textbf{\te{జలుబు}} (\emph{jalubu}) — \textquotedblleft{}a cold\textquotedblright{}, the kind with a runny nose.

\textbf{\te{నాకు} \te{జలుబు} \te{చేసింది}} — \textquotedblleft{}I have caught a cold\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}a cold has done to me\textquotedblright{}. Telugu keeps this apart from \textbf{\te{చలి}}, the cold of the weather.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The illness, next to the weather word you already have.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jalubu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jalubu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{nāku jalubu cēsindi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for where to, then the Telugu for have you eaten, then say \emph{jalubu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{జలుబు} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A cold, a runny nose\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[mandu]{\te{మందు} (mandu) — medicine}

\label{lesson:TE-C92-medicine}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for have you eaten, then the Telugu for a cold.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{మందు}}
\textbf{\te{మందు}} (\emph{mandu}) — \textquotedblleft{}medicine\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\te{మందు} \te{వేసుకోండి}} — \textquotedblleft{}please take the medicine\textquotedblright{}. Telugu \emph{puts on} a medicine, where English \emph{takes} it.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The cure, and the verb Telugu uses for taking it.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mandu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mandu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{mandu vēsukōṇḍi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for have you eaten, then the Telugu for a cold, then say \emph{mandu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{మందు} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Medicine\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[āsupatri]{\te{ఆసుపత్రి} (āsupatri) — a hospital}

\label{lesson:TE-C92-hospital}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for a cold, then the Telugu for medicine.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{ఆసుపత్రి}}
\textbf{\te{ఆసుపత్రి}} (\emph{āsupatri}) — \textquotedblleft{}a hospital\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\te{ఆసుపత్రి} \te{ఎక్కడ}?} — \textquotedblleft{}where is the hospital?\textquotedblright{}, with the \textbf{\te{ఎక్కడ}} you already ask places with.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A place to ask the way to when it matters most.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āsupatri}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āsupatri}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{āsupatri ekkaḍa?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for a cold, then the Telugu for medicine, then say \emph{āsupatri} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{ఆసుపత్రి} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A hospital\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[gāyaṁ]{\te{గాయం} (gāyaṁ) — a wound, an injury}

\label{lesson:TE-C92-wound}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for medicine, then the Telugu for a hospital.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{గాయం}}
\textbf{\te{గాయం}} (\emph{gāyaṁ}) — \textquotedblleft{}a wound, an injury\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\te{గాయం} \te{అయింది}} — \textquotedblleft{}I have been hurt\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}a wound has happened\textquotedblright{}. Like a wedding, an injury is something that happens.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A way to say you are hurt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gāyaṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gāyaṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{gāyaṁ ayindi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for medicine, then the Telugu for a hospital, then say \emph{gāyaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{గాయం} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A wound, an injury\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[nīrasaṁ]{\te{నీరసం} (nīrasaṁ) — weakness, lethargy}

\label{lesson:TE-C92-weakness}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for a hospital, then the Telugu for a wound.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{నీరసం}}
\textbf{\te{నీరసం}} (\emph{nīrasaṁ}) — \textquotedblleft{}weakness, lethargy\textquotedblright{}, the drained feeling after a fever.

\textbf{\te{నాకు} \te{నీరసంగా} \te{ఉంది}} — \textquotedblleft{}I feel weak\textquotedblright{}, in the frame of \textbf{\te{అలసటగా}} and \textbf{\te{దాహంగా}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A cold, medicine, a hospital, a wound, weakness: enough for a visit to the doctor.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nīrasaṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nīrasaṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{nāku nīrasaṁgā undi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for a hospital, then the Telugu for a wound, then say \emph{nīrasaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{నీరసం} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Weakness, lethargy\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
